cards.text: It's the Feast of Tabernacles, and Jesus has been teaching in the temple courts (John 7:14). Once again He tells the people, "I am the light of the world." Friend, after YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, when somebody says light, I'm LISTENING.

cards.question: Jesus says He is the light of the world. What does He promise whoever follows Him?

answers.text: They will never walk in the darkness
They will never be hungry again
They will never be troubled again

cards.text: Then the Pharisees, a group of strict religious leaders, push back. They say His words don't hold up, and they tell Him exactly why.

cards.question: What's the Pharisees' complaint about what Jesus just said?

answers.text: He is teaching on the Sabbath
He never studied with a teacher

cards.question: Jesus agrees with the Pharisees that His testimony about Himself is not valid.

cards.text: Jesus says His testimony IS valid, because He knows where He came from and where He's going. But they don't know where He came from or where He's going.
Then Jesus tells them they judge according to the flesh. As for Him, He judges no one.

cards.question: Jesus says that even if He does judge, His judgment is true. Why?

answers.text: He is with the Father who sent Him
He knows the Law better than anyone
The people in the temple agree with Him

cards.text: Now Jesus goes right to their own Law. Friend, nothing ends an argument faster than somebody reading your OWN group chat back to you.

cards.question: Their Law says the testimony of ___ men is valid. Jesus has that many: Himself and the ___.
The Pharisees ask Jesus, "Where is Your Father?" What does He tell them?

answers.text: They'd know His Father if they knew Him
His Father is back home in Nazareth
His Father will come to the temple soon

cards.text: Jesus says all this while teaching in the temple courts, near the treasury. Out in the open, and nobody lays a hand on Him.

cards.question: No one seized Jesus, because His ___ had not yet come.

cards.text: Again Jesus tells them He's going away. They'll look for Him, but they will die in their sin.

cards.question: Jesus tells them they will be able to come where He is going.

cards.text: That line sends the Jews into a huddle. They're trying to work out where He could possibly be going.

cards.question: Jesus said, "Where I am going, you cannot come." What do the Jews wonder?

answers.text: Whether He is going back to Galilee
Whether He will go teach the Greeks

cards.text: Jesus answers by telling them where everybody's from: "You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world."

cards.question: Jesus warns them they will die in their sins unless they ___ that He is the One.
The Jews ask Jesus, "Who are You?" What does He answer?

answers.text: Just what He's told them from the beginning
A prophet like Moses sent to Israel
The son of Joseph from Nazareth

cards.text: Jesus says He has much to say about them and much to judge. But the One who sent Him is truthful, and what Jesus has heard from Him, He tells the world.

cards.question: The Jews understand that Jesus is telling them about the Father.

cards.text: They missed who He meant, and no judgment here, friend: when somebody texts me "he called," I spend TWENTY MINUTES guessing WHICH he. So Jesus tells them that once they have lifted up the Son of Man, then they will know that He is the One.

cards.question: Jesus says that once they've lifted up the Son of Man, they'll know who He is. What else will they know about Him?

answers.text: He does nothing on His own
He acts on His own authority

cards.text: Jesus says the One who sent Him is with Him and has not left Him alone. After my years in that drawer, friend, that line hits me right in the apron.

cards.question: Jesus says the Father has not left Him alone, because He ___ does what pleases Him.
Jesus keeps speaking about the Father who sent Him. As He speaks these things, what do many do?

cards.text: And that's where we pull this batch out of the oven, friend. But keep that apron ON, because this conversation is NOT finished.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'They missed who He meant,' which tells John 8:27. Then it tells John 8:28. The card cites only John 8:28, so its citation is narrower than what it uses. It should be John 8:27-28.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Stop 2's choice cards follow a repeating cycle: true_false, multiple_choice, fill_blank, multiple_choice, then the same four again. Stop 1 also ends in a strict multiple_choice / fill_blank alternation (cards 8, 10, 11, 13). The question types follow a formula instead of being chosen for each card.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: 'That line sends the Jews into a huddle' says the Jews are talking among themselves. John 8:22 says only that 'the Jews began to ask' and doesn't say who they ask. The card fills in who is being spoken to.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin is only funny on four of the 28 cards (stop 1 cards 1 and 9, stop 2 cards 10 and 12). Most story cards are plain narration with no reaction, comparison, disbelief or self-deprecation. Examples are stop 1 cards 3, 6, 7 and 12, and stop 2 cards 1, 3, 5 and 8. Stop 2 runs from card 1 to card 9 without a laugh. Moments like the Pharisees calling His testimony invalid, or the Jews asking 'Will He kill Himself' (with respect for their situation), could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact. These cards read like a pleasant narrator.

rule.text: Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells no verse, which the docs allow when the last verse was asked on a choice card. It still cites John 8:30. The citation rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, and this card tells none.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the 'story isn't over' line, what should its verses field cite: the passage's last verse, the stop's range, or nothing (null)?
